extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for patent examiners (and practitioners responding to Office actions) on applying 35 U.S.C. 101/102/103 and related rules: how to identify, articulate, and overcome rejections and objections, determine effective filing dates and applicable prior art, and handle procedural matters (reconsideration, provisional rejections, form paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent application of patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The same standard of patentability applied in the examination of claims must be the same throughout the Office. All requirements for patentability (e.g., novelty, usefulness and unobviousness, as provided in 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, and 103) must be met before a claim is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mere fact that a claim recites in detail all of the features of an invention (i.e., is a “picture” claim) is never, in itself, justification for the allowance of such a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preponderance of the evidence standard for rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The standard to be applied in all cases is the 'preponderance of the evidence' test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner should reject a claim if, in view of the prior art and evidence of record, it is more likely than not that the claim is unpatentable. An application should not be allowed unless and until issues pertinent to patentability have been raised and resolved in the course of examination and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive handling of defects in form or omission of a limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application discloses patentable subject matter but claims in their present form cannot be allowed because of defects in form or omission of a limitation, the examiner should not stop with a bare objection or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's action should be constructive in nature and when possible should offer a definite suggestion for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noting patentable subject matter disclosed but not claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner is satisfied that patentable subject matter has been disclosed and the record indicates that the applicant intends to claim such subject matter, the examiner may note in the Office action that certain aspects or features have not been claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may indicate that if properly claimed such claims may be given favorable consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration after applicant reply (37 CFR 1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After reply by applicant or patent owner to a non-final action, the application or patent under reexamination will be reconsidered and again examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are rejected, or objections or requirements made, applicant or patent owner will be notified in the same manner as after the first examination. Applicant may reply in the same manner provided in § 1.111, with or without amendment, unless the Office action indicates that it is made final (§ 1.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between rejection and objection
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to grant claims because the subject matter as claimed is considered unpatentable is a 'rejection.' If the form of the claim (as distinguished from its substance) is improper, an 'objection' is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection (involving merits) is subject to review by the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences, while an objection, if persisted, may be reviewed only by way of petition to the Commissioner. Formal matters should not be combined in appeals to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of prior art; use best available art
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art rejections should ordinarily be confined strictly to the best available art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made where: (A) propriety depends on a particular interpretation of a claim; (B) a claim is met only in terms by a reference which does not disclose the inventive concept involved; or (C) the most pertinent reference seems likely to be antedated by a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration. Such rejections should be backed up by the best other art rejections available. Merely cumulative rejections should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation) and 103 (obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: For anticipation under 35 U.S.C. 102, the reference must teach every aspect of the claimed invention either explicitly or impliedly; any feature not directly taught must be inherently present. For a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103, reference teachings must be modified to meet the claims and the modification must be one which would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art at the time the invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2131-2146 for guidance on patentability determinations under 102 and 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the effective filing date of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules to determine the effective filing date include: (A) continuation/divisional under 35 U.S.C. 120 get earliest filing date in the line if 120 satisfied; (B) continuation-in-part claims not supported by parent have date of new application, claims fully supported under 112 by earlier parent have parent's date; (C) claiming foreign priority under 119(a)-(d) — effective filing date is the U.S. filing date unless (A) or (B) applies (foreign filing date not effective filing date though may overcome certain references); (D) claiming priority under 119(e) from a provisional gives the provisional filing date as effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related MPEP sections for PCT/371 specifics and differences between 111(a) and 371 filing types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining which subsection of 35 U.S.C. 102 applies (102(a),(b),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a printed publication or patent is found to disclose the claimed invention, the examiner should determine whether the rejection should be made under 35 U.S.C. 102(a), (b), or (e) by determining the effective filing date of the application and comparing with the date of the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the issue/publication date of the reference (including rules for weekend/holiday cutoff and that a magazine is effective as of the date it reached the addressee). If the publication/issue date is more than 1 year prior to effective filing date, 102(b) applies. If too recent for 102(b), consider 102(e): the reference must be a U.S. patent (or SIR) with a filing date earlier than the application's effective filing date and have a different inventive entity. If 102(e) does not apply, consider 102(a) where the reference has a publication date earlier and is not applicant's own work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the reference issue or publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must determine the issue or publication date of the reference so a proper comparison can be made with the application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the last day of the year dated from the date of publication falls on a Saturday, Sunday or Federal holiday, the publication is not a statutory bar under 102(b) if the application was filed on the next succeeding business day. See MPEP § 2124/2126/2128 for relevant case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming a 35 U.S.C. 102(b) rejection (printed publication or patent more than 1 year prior)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(b) can be overcome by: (A) persuasively arguing that the claims are patentably distinguishable from the prior art; (B) amending the claims to patentably distinguish; or (C) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) or 120 by amending the specification to specifically reference a prior application in accordance with 37 CFR 1.78(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming a 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e) can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentable distinction; (B) amending claims; (C) filing a 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit/declaration (showing the reference invention is not by 'another'); (D) filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration showing prior invention if the reference is not a U.S. patent (subject to limitations); (E) perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d); (F) perfecting priority under 119(e) or 120 by amending the specification per 37 CFR 1.78(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the claims of the reference and the application are directed to the same invention or are obvious variants, a 1.131 affidavit is not acceptable; consider double patenting or interference. If common assignee/inventor exists, a double patenting rejection must be made. If no common assignee/inventor and 102(e) is the only possible rejection, consider whether an interference should be declared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoming a 35 U.S.C. 102(a) rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: A rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(a) can be overcome by: (A) arguing patentable distinction; (B) amending claims; (C) filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit/declaration; (D) filing a 37 CFR 1.132 affidavit/declaration showing the reference invention is not by 'another'; (E) perfecting foreign priority under 119(a)-(d); (F) perfecting priority under 119(e) or 120 by amending the specification per 37 CFR 1.78(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) (abandonment of the invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), abandonment of the 'invention' (distinct from abandonment of an application) results in loss of right to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2134 for case law setting forth criteria for abandonment under 102(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(d) (foreign patenting statutory bar)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(d) establishes four conditions which, if all are present, establish a statutory bar against granting a patent in the U.S.: (A) the foreign application was filed >12 months before U.S. effective filing date; (B) filed by same applicant/legal representatives/assigns; (C) foreign application actually issued as a patent or inventor's certificate before U.S. filing; (D) the same invention is involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for an issued foreign patent for 102(d) prior art only if reasonable possibility exists that a foreign patent covering the same subject matter has been granted before the U.S. effective filing date. The document must be a patent or inventor's certificate, not merely a published application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection for copending U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copending U.S. patent application discloses subject matter which would anticipate the claims in another pending U.S. application having a different inventive entity, the examiner should determine whether a provisional 102(e) rejection can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If at least one common inventor exists between the applications or they are commonly assigned and the effective filing dates are different, a provisional rejection of the later-filed application should be made (based on presumption of future patenting). This provisional rejection may be overcome by 37 CFR 1.132 or 1.131 showings, or by abandoning and filing a new application containing both subject matters. A provisional rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling copending applications with no common inventor or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no common assignee or common inventor, the confidential status of applications under 35 U.S.C. 122 must be maintained and no rejection can be made relying on the earlier filed application as prior art under 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing dates are within 6 months (3 months for simple subject matter), interference may be proper. Otherwise the application with the earliest effective filing date must be allowed to issue; after publication the allowed application can be used as a reference under 102(e) in the still-pending application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) (applicant not the inventor)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(f) bars issuance of a patent where an applicant did not invent the subject matter being claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must presume the applicants are the proper inventors unless there is proof that another made the invention and that applicant derived the invention from the true inventor. See MPEP §§ 2137–2137.02 for substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) (priority of invention/pre-existing U.S. invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 102(g) bars issuance of a patent where another made the invention in the United States before applicant and had not abandoned, suppressed, or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section forms a basis for interference practice. In determining priority consider dates of conception and reduction to practice and the reasonable diligence of one who was first to conceive and last to reduce to practice. See MPEP Chapter 2300 and §§ 2138–2138.06 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs and statutory citation in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs (¶ 7.07–¶ 7.14, ¶ 7.15 etc.) should be used when making appropriate rejections, and the particular part of the reference relied upon should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute (35 U.S.C. 102) is required to be re-cited only in first actions on the merits and final rejections. Paragraph ordering requirements and which paragraphs must precede others are specified (e.g., ¶ 7.07 must precede ¶ 7.08–¶ 7.14 where indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for additional information on public use or sale (¶ 7.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: When an issue of public use or on-sale activity has been raised, the examiner may require additional information sufficient for the examiner to consider patentability under 35 U.S.C. 102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information sought should be restricted to what is reasonably necessary. A 1- or 2-month time period should be set for reply unless part of an Office action with a shortened statutory period; failure to reply will result in abandonment. If sufficient evidence exists to establish a prima facie case, use form paragraph 7.16 to make a rejection under 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language for rejections should be unequivocal
rubrics_metrics.description: The language to be used in rejecting claims should be unequivocal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 707.07(d) for guidance. Rejections should clearly identify the statutory basis and the prior art parts relied upon to support the rejection.
